1. A split pipe clamp comprising:

a first frame half and a second frame half joined at a hinge end by a hinge and releasably joined at a latch end by a latch, the first frame half and the second frame half defining, in a closed condition, a frame having an annular guide and three radial guides;

three jaw carriages, each jaw carriage being slidable radially in a respective one of the three radial guides and carrying a jaw pad, each jaw pad being pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage and having a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame;

a segmented cam ring received in the annular guide, the segmented cam ring comprising a first cam ring segment carried by the first frame half and a second cam ring segment carried by the second frame half, the first cam ring segment and the second cam ring segment having complementary coupling faces at the hinge end and complementary coupling faces at the latch end, the complementary coupling faces at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces at the latch end engaging one another as the first frame half and the second frame half are closed such that in the closed condition the first cam ring segment and the second cam ring segment rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring;

three oblique slots in the segmented cam ring and a follower on each jaw carriage received in a respective one of the three oblique slots, each oblique slot being inclined to a radial direction of the frame such that rotation of the coupled ring through a stroke advances the three jaw carriages inwardly in synchronism;

a wedge movable by the latch and positioned to bear on a ring drive face of the segmented cam ring, such that movement of the latch toward a closed position drives the wedge against the ring drive face and rotates the coupled ring through the stroke; and

a carriage return spring biasing each jaw carriage outwardly, such that release of the latch permits the carriage return springs to retract the jaw carriages.

2. The split pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the latch comprises a latch handle and a force-limiting spring stack in a drive train between the latch handle and the wedge, the force-limiting spring stack being arranged such that travel of the latch handle after all three jaw pads have contacted a pipe received in the frame compresses the force-limiting spring stack rather than advancing one of the jaw carriages farther inwardly than the others.

3. The split pipe clamp of claim 2, wherein the latch further comprises a latch housing and an indicator pin coupled to the force-limiting spring stack, the indicator pin being movable relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the force-limiting spring stack enters a predetermined compression range.

4. The split pipe clamp of claim 3, wherein the indicator pin is displaced by compression of the force-limiting spring stack independently of a diameter of the pipe received in the frame and independently of the position of the jaw carriages in the radial guides.

5. The split pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the latch has a first position in which the first frame half and the second frame half are held closed around a pipe received in the frame with the jaw carriages retracted, and a second, over-center position in which the wedge bears on the ring drive face and the coupled ring has been rotated through the stroke.

6. The split pipe clamp of claim 5, wherein in the second position a reaction transmitted from the wedge to the latch acts to hold the latch in the second position.

7. The split pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the followers and the oblique slots transmit outward movement of the jaw carriages under the carriage return springs into return rotation of the coupled ring when the latch is released, whereby the three jaw pads retract from a pipe received in the frame together.

8. The split pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the three oblique slots have the same inclination such that rotation of the coupled ring through a given angle advances the three jaw carriages by equal radial increments and the frame takes up a position centered on a pipe received in the frame.

9. The split pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein each jaw pad is pivotable on its jaw carriage such that the concave bearing face aligns itself with an outer surface of a pipe received in the frame, whereby the split pipe clamp grips pipes of different diameters within a radial travel of the jaw carriages without an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter.

10. The split pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the annular guide comprises an arcuate portion in the first frame half and an arcuate portion in the second frame half, the two arcuate portions registering with one another in the closed condition, each arcuate portion retaining the respective cam ring segment against radial displacement while permitting circumferential movement of that cam ring segment.

11. The split pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein the complementary coupling faces at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces at the latch end separate from one another when the latch is released and the first frame half and the second frame half are swung apart about the hinge, the first cam ring segment remaining with the first frame half and the second cam ring segment remaining with the second frame half.

12. The split pipe clamp of claim 1, further comprising a mounting boss on the frame outside the annular guide and arranged to support a sensor, a tool, or a conduit, the mounting boss being connected neither to the segmented cam ring nor to any of the jaw carriages.

13. The split pipe clamp of claim 1, wherein each of the first frame half and the second frame half is semicircular, and wherein the three jaw carriages are distributed around the frame in the closed condition such that the three jaw carriages approach a pipe received in the frame from three different directions.

14. A pipe-mounted equipment assembly comprising:

a split pipe clamp comprising a first frame half and a second frame half joined at a hinge end by a hinge and releasably joined at a latch end by a latch, the first frame half and the second frame half defining, in a closed condition, a frame having an annular guide and three radial guides; three jaw carriages, each jaw carriage being slidable radially in a respective one of the three radial guides and carrying a jaw pad, each jaw pad being pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage and having a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame; a segmented cam ring received in the annular guide and comprising a first cam ring segment carried by the first frame half and a second cam ring segment carried by the second frame half, the first cam ring segment and the second cam ring segment having complementary coupling faces at the hinge end and complementary coupling faces at the latch end that engage one another as the first frame half and the second frame half are closed such that in the closed condition the first cam ring segment and the second cam ring segment rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring; three oblique slots in the segmented cam ring and a follower on each jaw carriage received in a respective one of the three oblique slots, each oblique slot being inclined to a radial direction of the frame such that rotation of the coupled ring through a stroke advances the three jaw carriages inwardly in synchronism; a wedge movable by the latch and positioned to bear on a ring drive face of the segmented cam ring; and a carriage return spring biasing each jaw carriage outwardly;

a mounting boss on the frame outside the annular guide, the mounting boss being connected neither to the segmented cam ring nor to any of the jaw carriages; and

equipment supported on the mounting boss, the equipment comprising at least one of a sensor, a tool, and a conduit.

15. The pipe-mounted equipment assembly of claim 14, wherein the latch comprises a latch handle, a latch housing, a force-limiting spring stack in a drive train between the latch handle and the wedge, and an indicator pin coupled to the force-limiting spring stack and movable relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the force-limiting spring stack enters a predetermined compression range.

16. The pipe-mounted equipment assembly of claim 14, wherein the latch has a first position in which the first frame half and the second frame half are held closed around a pipe received in the frame with the jaw carriages retracted, and a second, over-center position in which the wedge bears on the ring drive face and the coupled ring has been rotated through the stroke.

17. A method of clamping a pipe, comprising:

opening a latch of a split pipe clamp and swinging a first frame half and a second frame half of the split pipe clamp apart about a hinge at a hinge end of the split pipe clamp, a first cam ring segment being carried by the first frame half and a second cam ring segment being carried by the second frame half;

placing the first frame half and the second frame half around a pipe;

closing the first frame half and the second frame half about the hinge so that complementary coupling faces at the hinge end and complementary coupling faces at a latch end engage one another and couple the first cam ring segment and the second cam ring segment into a coupled ring received in an annular guide of the split pipe clamp;

moving the latch to a first position in which the first frame half and the second frame half are held around the pipe with jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp retracted;

moving the latch to a second, over-center position, thereby driving a wedge against a ring drive face of the coupled ring and rotating the coupled ring through a stroke; and

advancing three jaw carriages of the split pipe clamp inwardly in synchronism by movement of a follower of each jaw carriage in a respective oblique slot of the coupled ring, until a jaw pad pivotally mounted on each jaw carriage seats on the pipe.

18. The method of claim 17, further comprising, after all three jaw pads have seated on the pipe, continuing to move a latch handle of the latch into the second position, thereby compressing a force-limiting spring stack in a drive train between the latch handle and the wedge rather than advancing one of the jaw carriages farther inwardly than the others.

19. The method of claim 18, further comprising observing displacement of an indicator pin relative to a fixed edge of a latch housing of the latch, the displacement indicating that the force-limiting spring stack has entered a predetermined compression range.

The method of claim 18, further comprising releasing the latch to unload the force-limiting spring stack, retracting the three jaw carriages outwardly under carriage return springs so that the followers turn the coupled ring back through the stroke and the three jaw pads lift from the pipe together, and thereafter swinging the first frame half and the second frame half apart about the hinge and removing the split pipe clamp from the pipe.

## View
Plan view of the segmented cam ring alone, removed from the frame, its two segments coupled, viewed along the axis of the ring. Black line work on white, no shading, all of it well inside the drawing area.

A flat annulus at the centre of the drawing area, bounded by an inner circular boundary and an outer circular boundary, is the segmented cam ring 20. The space inside the inner boundary is empty.

Three elongated openings pass through the annulus, one near the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right, spaced from one another and from both joints. Each is an oblique slot 34, drawn as a long narrow opening with rounded ends, lying within the width of the annulus and clearly inclined to the radius at its own position, so that one end of the slot is nearer the inner boundary and the other nearer the outer boundary. All three are inclined alike.

Near the right joint, the outer boundary of the second cam ring segment 24 runs for a short distance as a straight surface that slants inward as it approaches that joint, so that the segment is shallower at the joint than a short distance away from it. That slanting surface is the ring drive face 36.

- 20 segmented cam ring: target the outer boundary of the annulus in the upper right region.

# FIG. 3

## View
Enlarged fragmentary section through one jaw carriage, the cutting plane containing the radial direction of that jaw carriage and the axis of the frame. Radially outward is toward the top of the view, and the axis direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, all of it well inside the drawing area.

## Geometry and relationships
A hatched body in section spans the upper part of the view. A groove is formed in its right portion and a channel in its left portion, and the two meet.

The groove is wider than it is deep, is bounded by the body on its radially outer side above and its radially inner side below, is closed at its right, and opens toward the left of the view. A lip projects downward from the radially outer wall at the mouth of the groove and reaches part way across the mouth, leaving the rest of the mouth open. That groove is the annular guide 18.

A hatched block lies in the groove, filling it in the radial direction with a small running clearance at the walls above and below, and held in the groove by the lip. That block is the segmented cam ring 20. It is interrupted by a rectangular opening that passes through it from left to right, so that a radially outer portion of its outline remains above the opening and a radially inner portion remains below the opening. That opening is the oblique slot 34.

The channel runs downward through the body from the mouth of the groove and opens at the underside of the body. That channel is the radial guide 38. A ledge projects into the channel from its left wall near the lower end.

A hatched block lies in the channel and fills its width, its lower end projecting below the body. That block is the jaw carriage 30. A post extends to the right from the upper end of that block, passes through the open part of the mouth and enters the opening in the segmented cam ring 20, its upper and lower sides facing the radially outer and radially inner sides of that opening. That post is the follower 32.

A flange projects from the left side of the jaw carriage 30 above the ledge, and a compression spring is drawn as a zigzag line from the underside of the flange down to the ledge. That spring is the carriage return spring 44.

Below the body, a further body is carried on the lower end of the jaw carriage 30 through a small circle centred on the joint between them, the circle being a pivot shown schematically. That body is the jaw pad 40, its lower face a concave arc opening downward.

## Numerals on this sheet
- 18 annular guide: target the wall of the groove above the block that lies in it.
- 20 segmented cam ring: target well inside the hatching of the block in the groove, above the opening.
- 30 jaw carriage: target well inside the hatching of the block in the channel, below the flange.
- 32 follower: target well inside the post.
- 34 oblique slot: target the open space of the opening, to the right of the post.
- 38 radial guide: target the right wall of the channel, below the mouth of the groove.
- 40 jaw pad: target well inside the lowest body, above its concave lower face.
- 44 carriage return spring: target the zigzag line.

# FIG. 4

## View
Enlarged fragmentary section of the latch, viewed as in FIG. 1, so that radially outward is toward the top of the view and the circumferential direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, all of it well inside the drawing area.

## Geometry and relationships
At the lower left of the drawing area a plain hatched body in section carries the parts shown. A shallow open channel in its upper face holds a hatched arcuate band that runs from the left edge of the view toward the middle. That band is the segmented cam ring 20. Near the right end of the band, its upper side runs for a short distance as a straight surface that slants downward toward the right. That slanting surface is the ring drive face 36.

To the right, a hatched enclosure in section stands on the plain body, with a left wall, a right wall and a top wall around an interior cavity, the cavity opening downward at the bottom of the enclosure above the right end of the band. That enclosure is the latch housing 58.

A block lies in the lower part of the cavity between the left and right walls, which guide it to move up and down in the view. Its lower left face slants at the same angle as the ring drive face 36 and bears against it, so that downward movement of the block drives the band to the left. That block is the wedge 52.

Above that block, within the cavity, a compression spring is drawn as a zigzag line running from the upper face of the wedge 52 up to a flat plate lying across the cavity. That spring is the force-limiting spring stack 54.

An elongated lever is pivoted to the latch housing 58 at a small circle in the upper right part of the cavity and extends upward and to the right, passing out above the right wall and ending well inside the drawing area. A short link joins the lever to the flat plate, so that the lever presses the plate downward. The lever leans to the right, past the upright, in the over-centre position. That lever is the latch handle 50.

A slender pin rises from the flat plate, passes through a hole in the top wall of the latch housing 58 and stands above that top wall. That pin is the indicator pin 56.

## Numerals on this sheet
- 16 latch: target the outer boundary of the enclosure at its lower right corner.
- 20 segmented cam ring: target well inside the hatching of the arcuate band, near the left edge of the view.
- 36 ring drive face: target the slanting surface on the upper side of the band, where the block bears on it.
- 50 latch handle: target well inside the lever, above the top wall of the enclosure.
- 52 wedge: target well inside the block in the lower part of the cavity.
- 54 force-limiting spring stack: target the zigzag line above that block.
- 56 indicator pin: target the part of the pin standing above the top wall.
- 58 latch housing: target well inside the hatching of the top wall of the enclosure.

Part names above are semantic identifiers only; the image carries no text, numerals, or labels.

# FIG. 3

## View
Enlarged fragmentary section through one jaw carriage, the cutting plane containing that carriage's radial direction and the frame axis. Radially outward is toward the top; the axis direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area.

## Geometry and relationships
A hatched body in section spans the upper part of the view, with a groove in its right portion and a channel in its left portion, the two meeting.

The groove is wider than deep, bounded by the body above and below, closed at its right and open toward the left. A lip projects downward from the upper wall at the mouth of the groove and reaches part way across it, leaving the rest of the mouth open. That groove is the annular guide 18.

A hatched block lies in the groove, filling it radially with a small running clearance above and below and held in by the lip. That block is the segmented cam ring 20. A rectangular opening passes through the block from left to right, leaving a portion of its outline above the opening and a portion below it. That opening is the oblique slot 34.

The channel runs downward from the mouth of the groove and opens at the underside of the body. That channel is the radial guide 38, and a ledge projects into it from its left wall near the lower end.

A hatched block lies in the channel and fills its width, its lower end projecting below the body. That block is the jaw carriage 30. A post extends to the right from its upper end, through the open part of the mouth and into the opening in the block above, its upper and lower sides facing the radially outer and radially inner sides of that opening. That post is the follower 32.

A flange on the left side of the jaw carriage 30 stands above the ledge, and a compression spring is drawn as a zigzag line from the underside of the flange down to the ledge. That spring is the carriage return spring 44.

Below the body, a further body hangs from the lower end of the jaw carriage 30 on a small circle that is a pivot shown schematically. That body is the jaw pad 40, its lower face a concave arc.

## Numerals on this sheet
- 18 annular guide: target the groove wall above the block lying in it.
- 20 segmented cam ring: target the hatching of the block in the groove, above the opening.
- 30 jaw carriage: target the hatching of the block in the channel, below the flange.
- 32 follower: target well inside the post.
- 34 oblique slot: target the open space of the opening, right of the post.
- 38 radial guide: target the right wall of the channel, below the groove mouth.
- 40 jaw pad: target well inside the lowest body.
- 44 carriage return spring: target the zigzag line.

# FIG. 4

## View
Enlarged fragmentary section of the latch, viewed as in FIG. 1, so that radially outward is toward the top and the circumferential direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area.

## Geometry and relationships
At the lower left a plain hatched body in section carries the parts shown. A shallow open channel in its upper face holds a hatched arcuate band running from the left edge of the view toward the middle. That band is the segmented cam ring 20. Near the right end of the band, its upper side runs for a short distance as a straight surface that slants downward toward the right. That slanting surface is the ring drive face 36.

To the right, a hatched enclosure in section stands on the plain body, with a left wall, a right wall and a top wall around a cavity that opens downward above the right end of the band. That enclosure is the latch housing 58.

A block lies in the lower part of the cavity between the left and right walls, which guide it up and down. Its lower left face slants at the same angle as the ring drive face 36 and bears against it, so that downward movement of the block drives the band to the left. That block is the wedge 52.

Above that block, a compression spring is drawn as a zigzag line running from the upper face of the wedge 52 up to a flat plate lying across the cavity. That spring is the force-limiting spring stack 54.

An elongated lever is pivoted to the latch housing 58 at a small circle in the upper right of the cavity and extends upward and to the right, passing out above the right wall and ending well inside the drawing area. A short link joins the lever to the flat plate, so the lever presses the plate downward. The lever leans right, past the upright, in the over-centre position. That lever is the latch handle 50.

A slender pin rises from the flat plate, passes through a hole in the top wall of the latch housing 58 and stands above it. That pin is the indicator pin 56.

Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5. The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, or a conduit that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. The mounting boss 70 is connected neither to the segmented cam ring 20 nor to any jaw carriage 30 and does not participate in the synchronization of the jaw carriages 30. Equipment carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.
The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 passes through the segmented cam ring 20 and is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that circumferential movement of the ring produces a radial displacement of anything constrained to follow the slot. The three oblique slots 34 have the same inclination, so that a given rotation of the coupled ring advances each jaw carriage 30 by the same radial increment. The inclination of the oblique slots 34 sets the ratio between the circumferential stroke of the coupled ring and the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch acts as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge of the latch can reach, in the illustrated embodiment on the segment adjacent the latch end, and it lies at an inclination to the direction in which that wedge advances, so that advance of the wedge moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.
FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30. The frame is channeled to form the annular guide 18, which receives the segmented cam ring 20 and retains it against radial and axial displacement while permitting it to move circumferentially. The annular guide 18 is formed in both frame halves, one arcuate portion of the annular guide 18 in each frame half, and the two arcuate portions register with one another in the closed condition to form a continuous annular path in which the coupled ring turns.

The frame is further formed with a radial guide 38 at the position of each jaw carriage 30. Each jaw carriage 30 is received in a respective radial guide 38 and is constrained by the radial guide 38 to move radially with respect to the frame. Each jaw carriage 30 carries a follower 32 that projects from the jaw carriage 30 into a respective one of the oblique slots 34 of the segmented cam ring 20. The follower 32 bears against the sides of the oblique slot 34.

The follower 32 is constrained in two ways at once. The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 confines the follower 32 to a path that is inclined to the radial direction. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. Because all three followers 32 are engaged in slots of the same inclination in one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism, by equal radial increments, for as long as the ring turns. The jaw pads therefore close on the pipe together.

At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands, and the contact is distributed along the face instead of being taken at one edge of it. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.

A carriage return spring 44 acts between each jaw carriage 30 and the frame so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward. When the latch 16 is released and the drive from the latch to the ring drive face 36 is removed, the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward, the followers 32 bear on the opposite sides of their oblique slots 34, and the coupled ring is turned back through its stroke. The jaws are thus retracted from the pipe by the same synchronized path, and the clamp 100 is left with its jaw carriages 30 retracted and ready for the next installation. Retraction of the jaw carriages 30 also clears the jaw pads 40 from the pipe before the frame halves are swung apart, so that the pipe surface is not scraped by a jaw pad 40 that is still bearing on it.

The following description of embodiments refers to the accompanying drawings. The same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout. Terms of direction are used with respect to the frame of the clamp: the axis of the frame is the axis about which the frame is annular in the closed condition and with which the axis of a clamped pipe substantially coincides, "inward" and "radially inward" mean toward that axis, "outward" and "radially outward" mean away from it, and "circumferential" means about that axis. These terms describe relationships within the clamp and do not require the clamp to be used in any particular attitude.

Overall arrangement

FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 in the closed condition around a pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. Each of the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 is semicircular, and the two frame halves together surround the pipe 90. The first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are joined at one end, referred to as the hinge end, by a hinge 14, and are releasably joined at the other end, referred to as the latch end, by a releasable latch 16. The hinge 14 permits the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 to be swung apart far enough for the clamp 100 to be passed sideways onto a pipe 90 that is already installed, so that the clamp 100 need not be threaded over a free end of the pipe 90. When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame that is annular about the axis of the clamp 100.

Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5. The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, or a conduit that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. The mounting boss 70 is connected neither to the segmented cam ring 20 nor to any jaw carriage 30 and does not participate in the synchronization of the jaw carriages 30. Equipment carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.

The segmented cam ring

FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20 of the clamp 100, drawn removed from the frame with its segments in the coupled condition. The segmented cam ring 20 comprises a first cam ring segment 22 and a second cam ring segment 24. The first cam ring segment 22 is carried by the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 is carried by the second frame half 12, so that each frame half carries one segment of the ring and each segment travels with its own frame half when the clamp 100 is opened.

The first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet at two places, one at the hinge end and one at the latch end. At the hinge end the two segments have complementary coupling faces 26, and at the latch end they have complementary coupling faces 28. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are circumferentially facing drive faces, each pair being shaped so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other through the joint. The faces are brought into engagement by the same motion that closes the frame halves: as the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are swung together about the hinge 14 and the latch 16 is engaged, the complementary coupling faces 26 close on one another at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 close on one another at the latch end.

Coupling the segments in this way solves a problem created by splitting the clamp. A clamp that must open from the side cannot carry a continuous drive ring across the split, and a divided drive must otherwise be operated separately in each half, with the result that the two halves advance their jaws by amounts that are not fixed relative to one another. Here the division of the ring is undone by the act of closing the clamp. In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring, and a circumferential input applied to either segment is carried around the whole ring. One input, applied at one point on one frame half, therefore reaches every jaw carriage 30 through a single kinematic element, and the relationship between the jaw carriages 30 is set by the geometry of the ring rather than by the way the clamp is operated. When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken automatically with each use and requires no separate assembly step.

The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 passes through the segmented cam ring 20 and is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that circumferential movement of the ring produces a radial displacement of anything constrained to follow the slot. The three oblique slots 34 have the same inclination, so that a given rotation of the coupled ring advances each jaw carriage 30 by the same radial increment. The inclination of the oblique slots 34 sets the ratio between the circumferential stroke of the coupled ring and the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch acts as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge of the latch can reach, in the illustrated embodiment on the segment adjacent the latch end, and it lies at an inclination to the direction in which that wedge advances, so that advance of the wedge moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.

The jaw carriages

FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30. The frame is channeled to form the annular guide 18, which receives the segmented cam ring 20 and retains it against radial and axial displacement while permitting it to move circumferentially. The annular guide 18 is formed in both frame halves, one arcuate portion of the annular guide 18 in each frame half, and the two arcuate portions register with one another in the closed condition to form a continuous annular path in which the coupled ring turns.

The frame is further formed with a radial guide 38 at the position of each jaw carriage 30. Each jaw carriage 30 is received in a respective radial guide 38 and is constrained by the radial guide 38 to move radially with respect to the frame. Each jaw carriage 30 carries a follower 32 that projects from the jaw carriage 30 into a respective one of the oblique slots 34 of the segmented cam ring 20. The follower 32 bears against the sides of the oblique slot 34.

The follower 32 is constrained in two ways at once. The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 confines the follower 32 to a path that is inclined to the radial direction. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. Because all three followers 32 are engaged in slots of the same inclination in one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism, by equal radial increments, for as long as the ring turns. The jaw pads therefore close on the pipe together.

At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands, and the contact is distributed along the face instead of being taken at one edge of it. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.

A carriage return spring 44 acts between each jaw carriage 30 and the frame so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward. When the latch 16 is released and the drive from the latch to the ring drive face 36 is removed, the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward, the followers 32 bear on the opposite sides of their oblique slots 34, and the coupled ring is turned back through its stroke. The jaws are thus retracted from the pipe by the same synchronized path, and the clamp 100 is left with its jaw carriages 30 retracted and ready for the next installation. Retraction of the jaw carriages 30 also clears the jaw pads 40 from the pipe before the frame halves are swung apart, so that the pipe surface is not scraped by a jaw pad 40 that is still bearing on it.

The latch and the force-limiting drive train

FIG. 4 shows the latch 16 in fragmentary section. The latch 16 includes a latch housing 58 mounted on the frame at the latch end, a latch handle 50 pivotally mounted on the latch housing 58, a wedge 52 movable in the latch housing 58, and a force-limiting spring stack 54 in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52. The wedge 52 is positioned so that its inclined face bears on the ring drive face 36 of the segmented cam ring 20.

The latch 16 has two engaged positions. In a first position, the latch 16 holds the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 closed around the pipe 90 but does not clamp it: the frame is captive on the pipe 90 and cannot fall away, while the jaw carriages 30 remain retracted under their carriage return springs 44. In a second, over-center position, the latch handle 50 has been carried past the point of maximum resistance, and the reaction transmitted back from the wedge 52 through the force-limiting spring stack 54 acts to hold the latch handle 50 in the second position rather than to open it. Movement of the latch handle 50 from the first position to the second position advances the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36. The inclined face of the wedge 52 converts that advance into circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20, and the coupled ring turns through its limited stroke, the extent of the stroke being set by the travel of the wedge 52 between the first and second positions of the latch 16.

The force-limiting spring stack 54 answers the problem of what becomes of the operator's remaining handle travel. The jaw pads 40 land on the pipe 90 at some point in the stroke that depends on the diameter of the pipe 90, and the latch handle 50 has still to be carried into its over-center position. If the drive train from the latch handle 50 to the wedge 52 were rigid, that remaining travel would be taken up by whatever part of the assembly yielded first, in practice by driving one jaw farther into the pipe 90 than the others and loading it far more heavily. Here the force-limiting spring stack 54 is the most compliant element of the drive train once the jaw pads 40 are seated. Additional travel of the latch handle 50 after all three jaw pads 40 have contacted the pipe 90 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54 rather than forcing one jaw carriage 30 farther inward than the others, and the clamping force delivered at the jaw pads 40 is accordingly determined by the compression of the force-limiting spring stack 54 rather than by how hard the operator pulls the latch handle 50. The force-limiting spring stack 54 comprises one or more resilient elements arranged in a stack whose combined rate and travel are chosen so that the stack is stiff enough to carry the load required to advance the jaw carriages 30 to the pipe 90, and yielding enough to absorb the remaining travel of the latch handle 50 over the intended range of pipe diameters.

An indicator pin 56 is coupled to the force-limiting spring stack 54 and projects from the latch housing 58. As the force-limiting spring stack 54 compresses, the indicator pin 56 moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing 58, and the position of the indicator pin 56 with respect to that fixed edge shows the operator when the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered a predetermined compression range. The predetermined compression range is the range of stack compression that corresponds to the clamping force for which the clamp 100 is intended. The indicator pin 56 therefore reports clamp loading mechanically, at the clamp itself and without any separate instrument, and what it reports is the state of the force-limiting spring stack 54. It is not a measurement of the diameter of the pipe 90 and is not derived from the position of the jaw carriages 30: a large pipe and a small pipe seat the jaw pads 40 at different points in the stroke of the coupled ring, but the indicator pin 56 shows the same predetermined compression range in each case when the same clamping force has been reached.

Operation

To install the clamp 100 on a pipe 90, the operator opens the latch 16 and swings the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 apart about the hinge 14. The first cam ring segment 22 stays with the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 stays with the second frame half 12, and the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are separated. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 90 from the side and closes them about the hinge 14. Closing the frame halves brings the complementary coupling faces 26 into engagement at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 into engagement at the latch end, coupling the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 into the coupled ring within the annular guide 18.

The operator then moves the latch 16 to its first position, in which the frame is held around the pipe 90 without clamping. The operator moves the latch handle 50 to the second, over-center position. The wedge 52 is driven against the ring drive face 36, the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the sides of the three oblique slots 34 drive the three followers 32, and the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism until the pivoting jaw pads 40 seat on the pipe 90. The remaining travel of the latch handle 50 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54, and the operator watches the indicator pin 56 move relative to the fixed edge of the latch housing 58 and so sees that the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered the predetermined compression range. The latch 16 is left in the over-center position and the clamp 100 is loaded on the pipe 90.

To remove the clamp 100, the operator releases the latch 16. The latch handle 50 comes back over center, the wedge 52 retreats from the ring drive face 36, and the force-limiting spring stack 54 is unloaded. The carriage return springs 44 then push the jaw carriages 30 radially outward, turning the coupled ring back through its stroke by way of the followers 32 in the oblique slots 34, so that all three jaw pads 40 lift from the pipe 90 together. Only then are the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 swung apart about the hinge 14 and the clamp 100 taken off the pipe 90. The clamp 100 is undamaged by the cycle and may be installed again on the same pipe or on a pipe of a different diameter within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

Variations

The frame halves, the segmented cam ring 20, the jaw carriages 30, and the latch 16 may be made of any materials having the strength and stiffness required for the loads to be carried. The hinge 14 may be any joint that allows the frame halves to swing apart about a fixed axis at the hinge end while holding the complementary coupling faces 26 in register when the halves are closed. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 may take any complementary shapes that transmit circumferential force between the segments and that come into engagement as the frame halves close and separate as they open. The force-limiting spring stack 54 lies in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52. The carriage return spring 44 of each jaw carriage 30 may act at any location on the jaw carriage 30, provided that it biases the jaw carriage 30 outward when the drive from the latch 16 is removed.

Features described above in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features described in connection with another, except where the context makes the combination impossible. The embodiments described are illustrative of the disclosed clamp and are not exhaustive of it, and the scope of protection is defined by the claims that follow rather than by any particular embodiment described here.

lines: At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands, and the contact is distributed along the face instead of being taken at one edge of it. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.

-A carriage return spring 44 acts between each jaw carriage 30 and the frame so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward. When the latch 16 is released and the drive from the latch to the ring drive face 36 is removed, the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward, the followers 32 bear on the opposite sides of their oblique slots 34, and the coupled ring is turned back through its stroke. The jaws are thus retracted from the pipe by the same synchronized path, and the clamp 100 is left with its jaw carriages 30 retracted and ready for the next installation. Retraction of the jaw carriages 30 also clears the jaw pads 40 from the pipe before the frame halves are swung apart, so that the pipe surface is not scraped by a jaw pad 40 that is still bearing on it.

draft/08-detailed-description.md:5:FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 in the closed condition around a pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. Each of the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 is semicircular, and the two frame halves together surround the pipe 90. The first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are joined at one end, referred to as the hinge end, by a hinge 14, and are releasably joined at the other end, referred to as the latch end, by a releasable latch 16. The hinge 14 permits the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 to be swung apart far enough for the clamp 100 to be passed sideways onto a pipe 90 that is already installed, so that the clamp 100 need not be threaded over a free end of the pipe 90. When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame that is annular about the axis of the clamp 100.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:7:Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:9:The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5. The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, or a conduit that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. The mounting boss 70 is connected neither to the segmented cam ring 20 nor to any jaw carriage 30 and does not participate in the synchronization of the jaw carriages 30. Equipment carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:13:FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20 of the clamp 100, drawn removed from the frame with its segments in the coupled condition. The segmented cam ring 20 comprises a first cam ring segment 22 and a second cam ring segment 24. The first cam ring segment 22 is carried by the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 is carried by the second frame half 12, so that each frame half carries one segment of the ring and each segment travels with its own frame half when the clamp 100 is opened.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:21:The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch acts as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge of the latch can reach, in the illustrated embodiment on the segment adjacent the latch end, and it lies at an inclination to the direction in which that wedge advances, so that advance of the wedge moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:25:FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30. The frame is channeled to form the annular guide 18, which receives the segmented cam ring 20 and retains it against radial and axial displacement while permitting it to move circumferentially. The annular guide 18 is formed in both frame halves, one arcuate portion of the annular guide 18 in each frame half, and the two arcuate portions register with one another in the closed condition to form a continuous annular path in which the coupled ring turns.
draft/08-detailed-description.md:37:FIG. 4 shows the latch 16 in fragmentary section. The latch 16 includes a latch housing 58 mounted on the frame at the latch end, a latch handle 50 pivotally mounted on the latch housing 58, a wedge 52 movable in the latch housing 58, and a force-limiting spring stack 54 in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52. The wedge 52 is positioned so that its inclined face bears on the ring drive face 36 of the segmented cam ring 20.

input.summary: Fixed all fifteen review findings. Removed the untraced assertions from the description, summary, and background (exclusive pipe contact and bore relationship, pad facing/lining materials, alternative follower forms, spring seating surfaces, mounting boss placement freedom and "bracket", latch repositioning along the pipe, absence of a separate securing element, slot inclination design teaching, lubrication, and the intermediate sliding member), deleted the centering result from claim 8, the description, and the background bridge sentence while keeping the title as given in the brief, and corrected the claim antecedents for the carriage return springs and the jaw carriage count. Resolved the three geometric contradictions: FIG. 3 now shows the oblique slot as an axial through-opening entered by an axially extending follower, matching FIG. 2; the annular guide is now a groove bounded radially above and below with a retaining lip at its mouth, matching the retention recited in the description and claim 10; and the FIG. 4 wedge now descends onto an inclined ring drive face so its inclined face actually converts wedge advance into circumferential ring movement. The stepped lap joints and the four dished washers were replaced with shape-neutral abutting coupling faces and a generic spring line, and the projecting lug was replaced with an inclined surface on the ring itself. FIG. 1 now shows the jaw pad as a separate pivoted member, and because that added numeral 40 to a full sheet, the mounting boss moved to a new focused sheet, FIG. 5, with the brief description of the drawings and the detailed description updated to match.
reasoning: Source-fidelity findings were fixed by deletion or by retreating to the disclosed function, never by weakening a claim element that the disclosure supports. The exclusivity sentence became a plain statement that the jaw pads carried at the inner ends of the carriages bear on the pipe; the pad material sentence, the follower form list, the spring seating surfaces, the boss placement freedom, the mechanical-advantage teaching, the lubrication clause, and the intermediate sliding member were removed outright, and the wedge variation sentence was replaced with the disclosed relationship that the spring stack lies between the handle and the wedge.

Claim 8 lost only the centering result clause; the equal-inclination and equal-radial-increment limitations remain, so the fallback still has independent value. The description keeps 'the jaw pads therefore close on the pipe together', which is the synchronized advance the inventor described, without asserting a centering outcome. The title stays as the brief specified it, since the brief is authority for the title only.

Claim antecedents: claim 1 and claim 14 now recite three carriage return springs, each biasing a respective one of the jaw carriages, so the later plural references in claim 1 and claim 7 have proper antecedent basis. Claim 17 now introduces the three jaw carriages once, at the first-position step, and later refers to 'the three jaw carriages'.

Slot orientation was resolved in favor of FIG. 2, the axial through-slot, because it is the orientation the plan view of the ring already showed and it needed no change to the description. FIG. 3 was conformed: the opening now passes through the ring block from left to right in a section whose left-right direction is the frame axis, and the follower is a post extending axially from the carriage into that opening with its sides facing the slot flanks. Nothing was added to the specification or claims to accommodate this; the text says only that the follower projects into the slot and bears on its sides.

Ring retention was fixed in the drawing rather than by relaxing the text. The annular guide is now a groove bounded by frame material on the radially outer and radially inner sides, closed at one end and open axially through a mouth partly covered by a lip, so the walls retain the ring radially, the lip retains it axially, and the mouth still lets the follower reach the slot. This matches the description and claim 10, which were left as filed.

The wedge interface was made a working wedge. FIG. 4 now has the wedge guided radially inward while the ring drive face is an inclined surface on the radially outer side of the ring near the latch end, so wedge advance and ring movement are in different directions and the inclined face does the conversion the description recites. Because the figures and the text must agree, the description sentence about the ring drive face now says it lies at an inclination to the direction in which the wedge advances; that is the wedge relationship the disclosure itself sets up by reciting a wedge driven against a drive face, not a new structure.

The lap joints and the four dished washers were removed because they carried technical substance the disclosure does not give. The joints are now plain complementary circumferentially facing surfaces, and the spring stack is drawn with the same neutral zigzag convention already used for the carriage return spring, matching the description's 'one or more resilient elements arranged in a stack'.

The lug carrying the ring drive face was replaced with a short inclined surface formed on the outer boundary of the second cam ring segment near the latch-end joint, so the face lives on the ring itself, as the disclosure says, without adding a discrete projection.

For the FIG. 1 coverage problem I redistributed rather than deleted. Adding the pivoted jaw pad 40 would have made nine numerals on FIG. 1, so the mounting boss moved to a new focused sectional sheet, FIG. 5, which also shows the annular guide and the cam ring so that the disclosed relationship, boss outside the annular guide and connected to neither the ring nor any carriage, is what the sheet actually depicts. No numeral definition, disclosed part, or specification text was removed to make room, and the drawings section and detailed description now reference FIG. 5.

All five briefs stay under the character limit and describe only positive bodies, contacts, openings, and paths. Endpoint targets use broad interior language such as 'well inside' or 'the hatching of', and repeated shapes are identified by stable positions (topmost, left, right, lowest) rather than ordinals whose direction could be read either way.
changes: draft/05-background.md: the bridging paragraph now reads 'so that the gripping elements advance together over a range of pipe sizes' in place of the centering statement.

draft/06-summary.md: removed the sentence asserting that the frame takes its position from the jaws rather than from a bore; the paragraph now states only that the pivoting concave jaw pads seat without a diameter-specific insert.
draft/07-drawings.md: added the brief description of FIG. 5, the fragmentary section through the frame at the mounting boss.

draft/08-detailed-description.md: replaced the exclusive-contact sentence; carriage paragraph now says each carriage carries a jaw pad 40 at its inner end; mounting boss paragraph limited to a sensor, a tool, or a conduit, placement-freedom clause deleted, boss now referenced to FIG. 5 and to the annular guide 18 and segmented cam ring 20; deleted the slot inclination design teaching and the shallower/steeper trade-off; ring drive face paragraph now states the inclination to the direction of wedge advance; follower form list replaced with the bearing function; centering clause deleted; jaw pad material sentence deleted; spring seating sentence replaced with a general acting-between statement; deleted the sliding/turning along the pipe clause, the 'without a separate securing element' clause, the repositioning clause in the operation section, the lubrication clause, and the intermediate sliding member variant; scraping rationale reduced to the disclosed clearing of the pads before opening.

draft/09-claims.md: claim 1 and claim 14 now recite three carriage return springs, each biasing a respective one of the jaw carriages; claim 8 ends at equal radial increments; claim 17 introduces the three jaw carriages once and later refers to them definitely.

figures/fig-01.md: mounting boss removed from the sheet and from the numeral list; each jaw carriage now carries a separate member joined at a pivot circle with a shallow concave face meeting the pipe, identified as the jaw pad 40; numerals now 100, 10, 12, 14, 16, 30, 40, 90.

figures/fig-02.md: stepped overlapping joints replaced with plain complementary circumferentially facing surfaces at both joints; projecting lug replaced with a short straight surface on the outer boundary of the second cam ring segment that slants inward toward the latch-end joint, identified as the ring drive face 36; numeral 36 target updated.

figures/fig-03.md: annular guide is now a groove bounded radially above and below, closed at one end, opening axially through a mouth partly covered by a lip that holds the ring in; the ring fills the groove radially with a running clearance; the oblique slot now passes through the ring from left to right; the follower is a post extending axially from the upper end of the carriage through the mouth into the slot; numeral targets for 18, 20, 32, 34 and 38 updated.

figures/fig-04.md: view orientation stated; the ring drive face is now a surface on the upper side of the band slanting downward to the right; the latch housing cavity opens downward over it; the wedge is guided up and down with its lower left face at the same slant, so its descent drives the band to the left; the spring stack is a neutral zigzag between the wedge and a plate above it, the handle link presses that plate downward, and the indicator pin rises from the plate through the top wall; numeral targets for 36, 52 and 54 updated.

figures/fig-05.md: new focused sectional sheet showing the mounting boss 70 standing radially outside the annular guide 18, with the segmented cam ring 20 in the groove and no part of the boss reaching into it; numerals 18, 20, 70.

This revision did not touch the point of distinction: claim 1 still requires that the cam ring be divided between the frame halves and be re-coupled at the hinge end and the latch end by the closing motion itself, so that one latch input reaches all three jaw carriages through a single coupled ring, and the Background still states the problem that feature solves. The only claim scope surrendered in this pass was the centering result clause at the end of claim 8, which was removed because no inventor passage states that result; the equal-inclination and equal-increment limitations that carry the same argument remain in that claim. The force-limiting spring stack and the load-reporting indicator pin, which report stack compression rather than jaw position or pipe diameter, remain in claims 2 to 4, 15, 18 and 19 as the second line of distinction. input.answer:
Every listed mechanical check and reviewer finding has been fixed, and the numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims, and figure briefs are synchronized.

**Source-fidelity fixes (text)**
- Deleted: exclusive pipe-contact and bore assertions; pad facing/lining and softer-than-pipe material; the pin/post/roller follower list; the spring seating surfaces; "bracket", "other equipment", and boss placement freedom; sliding or turning the clamp in the first latch position; the "no separate securing element" assertion; the slot inclination design teaching and mechanical-advantage trade-off; lubrication of sliding parts; and the intermediate sliding member variant, replaced by the disclosed statement that the spring stack lies between handle and wedge.
- Centering removed from claim 8, from the description, and from the Background bridge sentence. The title stands as the brief gives it.
- Claim 1 and claim 14 now recite three carriage return springs, each biasing a respective jaw carriage; claim 17 introduces the three jaw carriages once.

**Geometric contradictions (drawings)**
- Slot orientation: FIG. 3 conformed to FIG. 2. The slot is an axial through-opening; the follower is a post extending axially from the carriage into it, its sides facing the slot flanks.
- Ring retention: the annular guide is now a groove bounded radially above and below, closed at one end, opening axially through a mouth partly covered by a lip, so the ring is retained radially and axially and can still be reached by the follower. Description and claim 10 unchanged.
- Wedge interface: the ring drive face is an inclined surface on the radially outer side of the ring near the latch end, and the wedge is guided radially inward with a matching slant, so its advance drives the ring circumferentially. The description now states that the drive face lies at an inclination to the direction of wedge advance, so text and figure agree.

**Shape-neutral depiction**
- Lap joints replaced with plain abutting circumferentially facing coupling faces; the four dished washers replaced with the same neutral spring convention used for the carriage return spring; the projecting lug replaced with a surface formed on the ring itself.

**Coverage**
- FIG. 1 now shows the jaw pad as a separate pivoted member (numeral 40). To keep that sheet at eight numerals without deleting anything, the mounting boss moved to a new focused sheet, FIG. 5, which shows the boss standing radially outside the annular guide with the cam ring in the groove. FIG. 5 is described in the Brief Description of the Drawings and referenced in the detailed description.

All 25 numerals remain unique and each appears on at least one sheet (FIG. 1: 8, FIG. 2: 7, FIG. 3: 8, FIG. 4: 8, FIG. 5: 3), every figure brief is under the character limit, the abstract is 149 words, and no notes, placeholders, or em dashes remain.

structured_output.summary: Fixed all fifteen review findings. Removed the untraced assertions from the description, summary, and background (exclusive pipe contact and bore relationship, pad facing/lining materials, alternative follower forms, spring seating surfaces, mounting boss placement freedom and "bracket", latch repositioning along the pipe, absence of a separate securing element, slot inclination design teaching, lubrication, and the intermediate sliding member), deleted the centering result from claim 8, the description, and the background bridge sentence while keeping the title as given in the brief, and corrected the claim antecedents for the carriage return springs and the jaw carriage count. Resolved the three geometric contradictions: FIG. 3 now shows the oblique slot as an axial through-opening entered by an axially extending follower, matching FIG. 2; the annular guide is now a groove bounded radially above and below with a retaining lip at its mouth, matching the retention recited in the description and claim 10; and the FIG. 4 wedge now descends onto an inclined ring drive face so its inclined face actually converts wedge advance into circumferential ring movement. The stepped lap joints and the four dished washers were replaced with shape-neutral abutting coupling faces and a generic spring line, and the projecting lug was replaced with an inclined surface on the ring itself. FIG. 1 now shows the jaw pad as a separate pivoted member, and because that added numeral 40 to a full sheet, the mounting boss moved to a new focused sheet, FIG. 5, with the brief description of the drawings and the detailed description updated to match.
reasoning: Source-fidelity findings were fixed by deletion or by retreating to the disclosed function, never by weakening a claim element that the disclosure supports. The exclusivity sentence became a plain statement that the jaw pads carried at the inner ends of the carriages bear on the pipe; the pad material sentence, the follower form list, the spring seating surfaces, the boss placement freedom, the mechanical-advantage teaching, the lubrication clause, and the intermediate sliding member were removed outright, and the wedge variation sentence was replaced with the disclosed relationship that the spring stack lies between the handle and the wedge.

Claim 8 lost only the centering result clause; the equal-inclination and equal-radial-increment limitations remain, so the fallback still has independent value. The description keeps 'the jaw pads therefore close on the pipe together', which is the synchronized advance the inventor described, without asserting a centering outcome. The title stays as the brief specified it, since the brief is authority for the title only.

Claim antecedents: claim 1 and claim 14 now recite three carriage return springs, each biasing a respective one of the jaw carriages, so the later plural references in claim 1 and claim 7 have proper antecedent basis. Claim 17 now introduces the three jaw carriages once, at the first-position step, and later refers to 'the three jaw carriages'.

Slot orientation was resolved in favor of FIG. 2, the axial through-slot, because it is the orientation the plan view of the ring already showed and it needed no change to the description. FIG. 3 was conformed: the opening now passes through the ring block from left to right in a section whose left-right direction is the frame axis, and the follower is a post extending axially from the carriage into that opening with its sides facing the slot flanks. Nothing was added to the specification or claims to accommodate this; the text says only that the follower projects into the slot and bears on its sides.

Ring retention was fixed in the drawing rather than by relaxing the text. The annular guide is now a groove bounded by frame material on the radially outer and radially inner sides, closed at one end and open axially through a mouth partly covered by a lip, so the walls retain the ring radially, the lip retains it axially, and the mouth still lets the follower reach the slot. This matches the description and claim 10, which were left as filed.

The wedge interface was made a working wedge. FIG. 4 now has the wedge guided radially inward while the ring drive face is an inclined surface on the radially outer side of the ring near the latch end, so wedge advance and ring movement are in different directions and the inclined face does the conversion the description recites. Because the figures and the text must agree, the description sentence about the ring drive face now says it lies at an inclination to the direction in which the wedge advances; that is the wedge relationship the disclosure itself sets up by reciting a wedge driven against a drive face, not a new structure.

The lap joints and the four dished washers were removed because they carried technical substance the disclosure does not give. The joints are now plain complementary circumferentially facing surfaces, and the spring stack is drawn with the same neutral zigzag convention already used for the carriage return spring, matching the description's 'one or more resilient elements arranged in a stack'.

The lug carrying the ring drive face was replaced with a short inclined surface formed on the outer boundary of the second cam ring segment near the latch-end joint, so the face lives on the ring itself, as the disclosure says, without adding a discrete projection.

For the FIG. 1 coverage problem I redistributed rather than deleted. Adding the pivoted jaw pad 40 would have made nine numerals on FIG. 1, so the mounting boss moved to a new focused sectional sheet, FIG. 5, which also shows the annular guide and the cam ring so that the disclosed relationship, boss outside the annular guide and connected to neither the ring nor any carriage, is what the sheet actually depicts. No numeral definition, disclosed part, or specification text was removed to make room, and the drawings section and detailed description now reference FIG. 5.

All five briefs stay under the character limit and describe only positive bodies, contacts, openings, and paths. Endpoint targets use broad interior language such as 'well inside' or 'the hatching of', and repeated shapes are identified by stable positions (topmost, left, right, lowest) rather than ordinals whose direction could be read either way.

Formalities check out against input/brief.md: title matches the working title exactly, cross-reference and government-support sections both read "Not applicable." (no priority claim, no federally sponsored research), no means-plus-function language appears in the claims, and the abstract runs ~144 words. No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, instructions, unresolved alternatives, or internal comments remain in any file. The numeral table is internally consistent: all 25 numerals are used in the description, every numeral in a figure brief appears in the table, and no numeral carries two meanings (gaps at 42/46/48/60/80 are harmless).

The core of the application traces cleanly: the two semicircular frame halves, hinge and releasable latch, three radial jaw carriages in radial guides, pivoting concave jaw pads with no diameter-specific insert, the segmented cam ring in the annular guide with one segment per half, the complementary coupling faces at hinge and latch ends that couple on closing, followers in oblique slots, the wedge driven by the latch against a ring drive face, the limited stroke, the outward-biasing carriage springs, the two latch positions including the over-center position, the force-limiting spring stack between handle and wedge, the indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing over a predetermined compression range, the install/remove method, and the optional mounting boss outside the annular guide that takes no part in synchronization. Independent claims 1, 14, and 17 are supported limitation-by-limitation, as are claims 2, 3, 5, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18 and 19.

Fourteen findings follow. Two are critical: an over-center reaction path recited in claim 6 and asserted in the detailed description with no source, and a block of "may be any material / any joint / any complementary shapes / any location" broadening sentences in the Variations paragraph that exist to justify renderer choices. The rest are added structural detail, added performance results, added drive-train members in the FIG. 4 brief, two cross-figure inconsistencies (indicator-pin reference frame, latch-handle attitude, annular-guide lip), and one claim-formality nit. In a closed condition the two frame halves define a frame having an annular guide and three radial guides. Three jaw carriages are each slidable radially in a respective one of the radial guides, and each jaw carriage carries a jaw pad that is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the segmented cam ring, each oblique slot being inclined to a radial direction of the frame so that rotation of the coupled ring through a stroke advances the three jaw carriages inwardly in synchronism. A wedge movable by the latch bears on a ring drive face of the segmented cam ring, so that movement of the latch toward a closed position rotates the coupled ring through the stroke, and a carriage return spring biases each jaw carriage outwardly so that releasing the latch retracts the jaws.
