The following description of embodiments refers to the accompanying drawings. The same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout. Terms of direction are used with respect to the frame of the clamp: the axis of the frame is the axis about which the frame is annular in the closed condition and with which the axis of a clamped pipe substantially coincides, "inward" and "radially inward" mean toward that axis, "outward" and "radially outward" mean away from it, and "circumferential" means about that axis. These terms describe relationships within the clamp and do not require the clamp to be used in any particular attitude.

Overall arrangement

FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 in the closed condition around a pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. Each of the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 is semicircular, and the two frame halves together surround the pipe 90. The first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are joined at one end, referred to as the hinge end, by a hinge 14, and are releasably joined at the other end, referred to as the latch end, by a releasable latch 16. The hinge 14 permits the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 to be swung apart far enough for the clamp 100 to be passed sideways onto a pipe 90 that is already installed, so that the clamp 100 need not be threaded over a free end of the pipe 90. When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame that is annular about the axis of the clamp 100.

Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5. The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, or a conduit that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. The mounting boss 70 is connected neither to the segmented cam ring 20 nor to any jaw carriage 30 and does not participate in the synchronization of the jaw carriages 30. Equipment carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.

The segmented cam ring

FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20 of the clamp 100, drawn removed from the frame with its segments in the coupled condition. The segmented cam ring 20 comprises a first cam ring segment 22 and a second cam ring segment 24. The first cam ring segment 22 is carried by the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 is carried by the second frame half 12, so that each frame half carries one segment of the ring and each segment travels with its own frame half when the clamp 100 is opened.

The first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet at two places, one at the hinge end and one at the latch end. At the hinge end the two segments have complementary coupling faces 26, and at the latch end they have complementary coupling faces 28. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are circumferentially facing drive faces, each pair being shaped so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other through the joint. The faces are brought into engagement by the same motion that closes the frame halves: as the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are swung together about the hinge 14 and the latch 16 is engaged, the complementary coupling faces 26 close on one another at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 close on one another at the latch end.

Coupling the segments in this way solves a problem created by splitting the clamp. A clamp that must open from the side cannot carry a continuous drive ring across the split, and a divided drive must otherwise be operated separately in each half, with the result that the two halves advance their jaws by amounts that are not fixed relative to one another. Here the division of the ring is undone by the act of closing the clamp. In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring, and a circumferential input applied to either segment is carried around the whole ring. One input, applied at one point on one frame half, therefore reaches every jaw carriage 30 through a single kinematic element, and the relationship between the jaw carriages 30 is set by the geometry of the ring rather than by the way the clamp is operated. When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken by the closing and opening of the frame halves.

The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 passes through the segmented cam ring 20 and is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that rotation of the coupled ring produces inward travel of its jaw carriage 30, the three oblique slots 34 being arranged so that the three jaw carriages 30 travel inwardly in synchronism. The inclination of the oblique slots 34 sets the ratio between the circumferential stroke of the coupled ring and the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch acts as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge of the latch can reach, and it lies at an inclination to the direction in which that wedge advances, so that advance of the wedge moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.

The jaw carriages

FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30. The frame is channeled to form the annular guide 18, which receives the segmented cam ring 20. The annular guide 18 retains the first cam ring segment 22 on the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 on the second frame half 12, and permits the coupled ring to move circumferentially.

The frame is further formed with a radial guide 38 at the position of each jaw carriage 30. Each jaw carriage 30 is received in a respective radial guide 38 and is constrained by the radial guide 38 to move radially with respect to the frame. Each jaw carriage 30 carries a follower 32 that projects from the jaw carriage 30 into a respective one of the oblique slots 34 of the segmented cam ring 20. The follower 32 bears against the sides of the oblique slot 34.

The follower 32 is constrained in two ways at once. The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 confines the follower 32 to a path that is inclined to the radial direction. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. Because all three followers 32 are engaged in oblique slots 34 of one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism for as long as the ring turns. The jaw pads 40 therefore close on the pipe together.

At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.

A carriage return spring 44 acts between each jaw carriage 30 and the frame so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward. When the latch 16 is released and the drive from the latch to the ring drive face 36 is removed, the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward and the jaw pads 40 are retracted from the pipe, and the clamp 100 is left with its jaw carriages 30 retracted and ready for the next installation. Retraction of the jaw carriages 30 clears the jaw pads 40 from the pipe before the frame halves are swung apart.

The latch and the force-limiting drive train

FIG. 4 shows the latch 16 in fragmentary section. The latch 16 includes a latch housing 58 mounted on the frame at the latch end, a latch handle 50 pivotally mounted on the latch housing 58, a wedge 52 movable in the latch housing 58, and a force-limiting spring stack 54 in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52. The wedge 52 is positioned so that its inclined face bears on the ring drive face 36 of the segmented cam ring 20.

The latch 16 has two engaged positions. In a first position, the latch 16 holds the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 closed around the pipe 90 but does not clamp it: the frame is captive on the pipe 90 and cannot fall away, while the jaw carriages 30 remain retracted under their carriage return springs 44. In a second, over-center position, the wedge 52 drives the segmented cam ring 20 and the pipe 90 is clamped. Movement of the latch handle 50 from the first position to the second position advances the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36. The inclined face of the wedge 52 converts that advance into circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20, and the coupled ring turns through its limited stroke, the stroke being limited by the travel available to the wedge 52 between the first and second positions of the latch 16.

The force-limiting spring stack 54 answers the problem of what becomes of the operator's remaining handle travel. The jaw pads 40 land on the pipe 90 at some point in the stroke that depends on the diameter of the pipe 90, and the latch handle 50 has still to be carried into its over-center position. If the drive train from the latch handle 50 to the wedge 52 were rigid, that remaining travel would be taken up by whatever part of the assembly yielded first, in practice by driving one jaw farther into the pipe 90 than the others and loading it far more heavily. Additional travel of the latch handle 50 after all three jaw pads 40 have contacted the pipe 90 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54 rather than forcing one jaw carriage 30 farther inward than the others.

An indicator pin 56 is coupled to the force-limiting spring stack 54 and projects from the latch housing 58. As the force-limiting spring stack 54 compresses, the indicator pin 56 moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing 58, and the position of the indicator pin 56 with respect to that fixed edge shows the operator when the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered a predetermined compression range. The predetermined compression range is the range of stack compression that corresponds to the clamping force for which the clamp 100 is intended. The indicator pin 56 therefore reports clamp loading mechanically, and what it reports is the state of the force-limiting spring stack 54. It is not a measurement of the diameter of the pipe 90.

Operation

To install the clamp 100 on a pipe 90, the operator opens the latch 16 and swings the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 apart about the hinge 14. The first cam ring segment 22 stays with the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 stays with the second frame half 12, and the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are separated. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 90 from the side and closes them about the hinge 14. Closing the frame halves brings the complementary coupling faces 26 into engagement at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 into engagement at the latch end, coupling the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 into the coupled ring within the annular guide 18.

The operator then moves the latch 16 to its first position, in which the frame is held around the pipe 90 without clamping. The operator moves the latch handle 50 to the second, over-center position. The wedge 52 is driven against the ring drive face 36, the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the sides of the three oblique slots 34 drive the three followers 32, and the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism until the pivoting jaw pads 40 seat on the pipe 90. The remaining travel of the latch handle 50 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54, and the operator watches the indicator pin 56 move relative to the fixed edge of the latch housing 58 and so sees that the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered the predetermined compression range. The latch 16 is left in the over-center position and the clamp 100 is loaded on the pipe 90.

To remove the clamp 100, the operator releases the latch 16. The latch handle 50 comes back over center, the wedge 52 retreats from the ring drive face 36, and the force-limiting spring stack 54 is unloaded. The carriage return springs 44 then push the jaw carriages 30 radially outward, so that the jaw pads 40 lift from the pipe 90. Only then are the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 swung apart about the hinge 14 and the clamp 100 taken off the pipe 90. The clamp 100 is undamaged by the cycle and may be installed again on the same pipe or on a pipe of a different diameter within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

Features described above in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features described in connection with another, except where the context makes the combination impossible. The embodiments described are illustrative of the disclosed clamp and are not exhaustive of it, and the scope of protection is defined by the claims that follow rather than by any particular embodiment described here.

# FIG. 1

## View
Plan view of the assembled split pipe clamp, closed around a pipe, viewed along the axis of the pipe. Black line work on white, no shading, no hatching, all of it well inside the drawing area.

## Geometry and relationships
A circle at the centre of the drawing area is the pipe 90, seen end on.

A ring of substantial width surrounds the pipe 90, drawn as an inner circular boundary and an outer circular boundary. The inner boundary is spaced outward from the pipe 90, leaving a visible gap between them.

Two radial joint lines divide the ring into two semicircular bodies, one joint at the left of the ring and one at the right of the ring. The upper semicircular body is the first frame half 10 and the lower semicircular body is the second frame half 12.

At the left joint is the hinge 14, drawn schematically as a small circle centred on that joint line with a short knuckle block reaching to it from each frame end.

At the right joint is the latch 16, drawn schematically as a rectangular block lying outside the outer boundary of the ring and bridging both frame ends, with an elongated lever extending from the block outward and away from the ring, on the side of the block remote from the second frame half 12, so that it stands as it does in FIG. 4.

Three jaw carriages 30 are spaced around the ring, one at the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right. Each is drawn as a block that crosses the inner boundary of the ring and reaches radially inward toward the pipe 90. The topmost jaw carriage lies on the first frame half 10; the other two lie on the second frame half 12.

Each jaw carriage 30 carries at its inner end a separate member, joined to the jaw carriage 30 at a small circle that is a pivot shown schematically. The inner face of that member is a shallow concave arc that meets the outer surface of the pipe 90. That member is the jaw pad 40.

## Numerals on this sheet
- 100 split pipe clamp: target the outer boundary of the ring in the upper right region.

# FIG. 2

## View
Plan view of the segmented cam ring alone, removed from the frame, its two segments coupled, viewed along the axis of the ring. Black line work on white, no shading, well inside the drawing area.

## Geometry and relationships
A flat annulus at the centre of the drawing area, bounded by inner and outer circular boundaries, is the segmented cam ring 20. The space inside the inner boundary is empty.

Two joints, one at the left and one at the right, divide the annulus into two arcuate segments. The upper segment is the first cam ring segment 22 and the lower segment is the second cam ring segment 24.

At the left joint the end of the first cam ring segment 22 and the end of the second cam ring segment 24 meet along plain complementary surfaces that face circumferentially. Those surfaces are the complementary coupling faces at the hinge end 26.

At the right joint the two segment ends meet in the same way, along plain complementary surfaces that face circumferentially. Those surfaces are the complementary coupling faces at the latch end 28.

Three elongated openings pass through the annulus, one near the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right, spaced from one another and from both joints. Each is an oblique slot 34, drawn as a long narrow opening with rounded ends, lying within the width of the annulus and clearly inclined to the radius at its own position, so that one end of the slot is nearer the inner boundary and the other nearer the outer boundary. In each slot the end nearer the inner boundary lies counterclockwise of the end nearer the outer boundary, as viewed in this figure, so that clockwise rotation of the ring, the sense in which the wedge drives it in FIG. 4, brings the inner portion of each slot to the circumferential position held by its outer portion.

Near the right joint, the outer boundary of the second cam ring segment 24 runs for a short distance as a straight surface that slants inward toward that joint. That slanting surface is the ring drive face 36.

## Numerals on this sheet
- 20 segmented cam ring: target the outer boundary of the annulus in the upper right.
- 22 first cam ring segment: target well inside the upper segment, in its upper left region.
- 24 second cam ring segment: target well inside the lower segment, at the bottom of the annulus.
- 26 complementary coupling faces at the hinge end: target the meeting surfaces at the left joint.
- 28 complementary coupling faces at the latch end: target the meeting surfaces at the right joint.
- 34 oblique slot: target well inside the opening near the top.
- 36 ring drive face: target the slanting surface on the outer boundary near the right joint.

# FIG. 3

## View
Enlarged fragmentary section through one jaw carriage, the cutting plane containing that carriage's radial direction and the frame axis. Radially outward is toward the top; the axis direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. The carriage return spring and its seats are shown schematically.

## Geometry and relationships
A hatched body in section spans the upper part of the view, with a groove in its right portion and a channel in its left portion, the two meeting.

The groove is wider than deep, bounded by the body above and below, closed at its right and open toward the left. That groove is the annular guide 18.

A hatched block lies in the groove, filling it radially with a small running clearance above and below. That block is the segmented cam ring 20. A rectangular opening passes through the block from left to right, leaving a portion of its outline above the opening and a portion below it. That opening is the oblique slot 34.

The channel runs downward from the mouth of the groove and opens at the underside of the body. That channel is the radial guide 38.

A hatched block lies in the channel and fills its width, its lower end projecting below the body. That block is the jaw carriage 30. A post extends to the right from its upper end, through the mouth of the groove and into the opening in the block lying in the groove, its upper and lower sides facing the sides of that opening. That post is the follower 32.

A compression spring is drawn as a zigzag line acting between the jaw carriage 30 and the wall of the channel so as to urge the jaw carriage 30 upward, that is, radially outward; its seats are shown schematically. That spring is the carriage return spring 44.

Below the body, a further body hangs from the lower end of the jaw carriage 30 on a small circle that is a pivot shown schematically. That body is the jaw pad 40, its lower face a concave arc.

# FIG. 4

## View
Enlarged fragmentary section of the latch, taken at the latch end and viewed along the axis of the frame from the side opposite that of FIG. 1, so that radially outward is toward the top, the circumferential direction runs left to right, and the right of the view lies circumferentially toward the first frame half 10, which lies outside this view. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. The flat plate is a spring seat shown schematically.

## Geometry and relationships
At the lower left a plain hatched body in section carries the parts shown; a shallow channel in its upper face holds a hatched arcuate band, the segmented cam ring 20, running from the left edge toward the middle. Near its right end the upper side of the band runs as a short straight surface slanting downward to the right, the ring drive face 36.

To the right, a hatched enclosure in section stands on the plain body, its left, right and top walls enclosing a cavity that opens downward above the right end of the band. That enclosure is the latch housing 58.

A block, the wedge 52, lies in the lower cavity between the left and right walls, which guide it up and down. Its lower left face slants at the same angle as the ring drive face 36 and bears on it, so downward movement of the wedge 52 drives the band to the left.

Above it, the force-limiting spring stack 54 is drawn as a zigzag compression spring line from the upper face of the wedge 52 to a flat plate across the cavity.

An elongated lever, the latch handle 50, is pivoted to the latch housing 58 at a small circle in the upper right of the cavity and extends up and to the right, passing out above the right wall and ending inside the drawing area. It bears on the flat plate and presses it downward, leaning right, past the upright, in the over-centre position.

A slender pin, the indicator pin 56, rises from the flat plate through a hole in the top wall of the latch housing 58 and stands above it.

## Numerals on this sheet
- 16 latch: place in free space to the lower right of the enclosure, its leader ending in the empty space beside the enclosure and the handle, so that it designates the latch assembly as a whole and not the wall designated 58.
- 20 segmented cam ring: target the hatching of the band at the left.
- 36 ring drive face: target the slanting surface on the band.
- 50 latch handle: target well inside the lever above the top wall.
- 52 wedge: target well inside the block in the cavity.
- 54 force-limiting spring stack: target the zigzag line.
- 56 indicator pin: target the part of the pin above the top wall.
- 58 latch housing: target the hatching of the top wall.

# FIG. 2

## View
Plan view of the segmented cam ring alone, removed from the frame, its two segments coupled, viewed along the axis of the ring. Black line work on white, no shading, well inside the drawing area.

## Geometry and relationships
A flat annulus at the centre of the drawing area, bounded by inner and outer circular boundaries, is the segmented cam ring 20. The space inside the inner boundary is empty.

Two joints, one at the left and one at the right, divide the annulus into two arcuate segments. The upper segment is the first cam ring segment 22 and the lower segment is the second cam ring segment 24.

At the left joint the ends of the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet along plain complementary surfaces facing circumferentially, the complementary coupling faces at the hinge end 26.

At the right joint the two segment ends meet in the same way, along plain complementary surfaces facing circumferentially, the complementary coupling faces at the latch end 28.

Three elongated openings pass through the annulus, one near the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right, spaced from one another and from both joints; those circumferential positions are shown schematically. Each is an oblique slot 34, a long narrow opening with rounded ends, lying within the width of the annulus and clearly inclined to the radius at its own position, so that one end is nearer the inner boundary and the other nearer the outer boundary. In each slot the end nearer the inner boundary lies counterclockwise of the end nearer the outer boundary, as viewed here, so that clockwise rotation of the ring, the sense in which the wedge drives it in FIG. 4, brings the inner portion of each slot to the circumferential position held by its outer portion.

Near the right joint, the outer boundary of the second cam ring segment 24 runs as a short straight surface slanting inward toward that joint, the ring drive face 36. The segment on which the ring drive face 36 is shown, and its position on the outer boundary, are shown schematically.

## Numerals on this sheet
- 20 segmented cam ring: target the outer boundary of the annulus in the upper right.
- 22 first cam ring segment: target well inside the upper segment, in its upper left.
- 24 second cam ring segment: target well inside the lower segment, at the bottom of the annulus.
- 26 complementary coupling faces at the hinge end: target the meeting surfaces at the left joint.
- 28 complementary coupling faces at the latch end: target the meeting surfaces at the right joint.
- 34 oblique slot: target well inside the opening near the top.
- 36 ring drive face: target the slanting surface near the right joint.

input.summary: Fixed all eight findings. Claim 6 and the description now state only that the annular guide retains the first cam ring segment on the first frame half and the second on the second frame half while permitting the coupled ring to move circumferentially, with no subdivision of the guide into arcuate portions. The description no longer says the oblique slots pass through the ring, and the through-opening stays a rendering convention with its depth marked schematic in FIG. 3. FIG. 2 now declares the segment and position chosen for the ring drive face as schematic, and the circumferential stations of the three slots as schematic; FIG. 1 declares the carriage positions and their apportionment between the halves as schematic. FIG. 4 now uses the broken-away convention above the band so its channel no longer contradicts the closed groove of FIG. 3 and FIG. 5, its numeral 16 is placed with no lead line and a freestanding arrow toward the assembly, and the Brief Description of FIG. 4 states the transverse section plane and the opposite viewing side. The duplicate pipe antecedents in claims 4, 5, 9, 12 and in the method's placing step are now definite.
reasoning: Claim 6 was recast to the retention relationship the disclosure supplies, that the ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame and one segment is carried by each frame half, rather than a guide divided into two arcuate portions each independently receiving its own segment. The description was changed in the same words so the claim has verbatim support, and the sentence about registering portions forming a continuous path is gone.

The through-slot assertion was deleted from the description so the text says only that each slot is inclined and drives its carriage inward. The opening still has to be drawn, so FIG. 3 now marks the depth of the opening schematic, which keeps the topology choice inside the brief where it belongs.

Three depiction choices that a drawing cannot avoid are now labeled as such in the briefs and nowhere else: which segment carries the ring drive face and where on the outer boundary it sits, the circumferential stations of the three slots, and the circumferential stations of the three carriages with their apportionment between the halves. The description and claims were left untouched on all three points, since they already speak only of a drive face on the ring and carriages distributed around the frame.

The FIG. 4 cross-section conflict was resolved with the broken-away convention rather than by relieving the outer wall of the guide, because relieving that wall at the latch end would be structure the disclosure never gives. The band's upper side is exposed by the break, the channel is left undesignated on that sheet, and FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 keep the groove closed on its radially outer side.

The FIG. 4 entry in the Brief Description now carries the transverse section plane and the statement that the view is taken from the side opposite FIG. 1. That matters because the drive sense is the crux of the mechanism: FIG. 2 fixes clockwise rotation as the sense the wedge drives, and a reader who assumed FIG. 4 was viewed from the FIG. 1 side would read the wedge as driving the ring the wrong way.

Numeral 16 on FIG. 4 no longer instructs a leader into blank space. It is placed with no lead line and a freestanding arrow pointing at the latch assembly, which keeps it distinct from the housing wall designated 58 without a leader that terminates on nothing.

The pipe antecedents were made definite in claims 4, 5, 9 and 12 and in the method's placing step, so the pipe introduced in claims 1, 10 and the method preamble is the only pipe in the set, matching claim 3, which was already correct.

Every brief was trimmed to stay within the character limit while the added qualifiers went in: 2778, 2785, 2708, 2794 and 1692 characters. Sheet counts remain 8, 7, 8, 8 and 3 with names identical to the numerals table, all 25 numerals still appear in the description and on at least one sheet, and the abstract is unchanged at 149 words.

figures/fig-02.md: added that the circumferential positions of the three slots are shown schematically and that the segment on which the ring drive face 36 is shown and its position on the outer boundary are shown schematically; condensed several sentences and numeral targets.

# Invention disclosure (the inventor's own words)

This is the ONLY authority for what the invention includes. Everything you claim must be supported here or in later messages from the user.

A reusable split pipe clamp has a first semicircular frame half and a second semicircular frame half joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end. Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame. Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter.

A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half. When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke. The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages. A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released.

The latch has a first position that holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second over-center position that drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge, so additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others. A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range. The indicator reports clamp loading mechanically and does not measure pipe diameter.

To install the clamp, an operator opens the latch, swings the frame halves apart, places them around a pipe, closes the frame, moves the latch to the holding position, and then moves the latch to the over-center position. The coupled cam ring advances all jaw carriages until the pivoting pads seat on the pipe. To remove the clamp, releasing the latch unloads the spring stack and the carriage springs retract the jaws before the frame halves are opened.

The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization. The disclosed essential relationship is that closure couples the ring segments and latch travel drives the coupled ring, while the oblique slots synchronize the radial jaw carriages and the force-limiting spring stack accommodates the remaining latch travel.

# Conversation so far

### USER

Here is my invention.

A reusable split pipe clamp has a first semicircular frame half and a second semicircular frame half joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end. Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame. Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter.

A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half. When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke. The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages. A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released.

A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge, so additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others. The coupled cam ring advances all jaw carriages until the pivoting pads seat on the pipe. The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization. The disclosed essential relationship is that closure couples the ring segments and latch travel drives the coupled ring, while the oblique slots synchronize the radial jaw carriages and the force-limiting spring stack accommodates the remaining latch travel.

1	The following description of embodiments refers to the accompanying drawings. The same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout. Terms of direction are used with respect to the frame of the clamp: the axis of the frame is the axis about which the frame is annular in the closed condition and with which the axis of a clamped pipe substantially coincides, "inward" and "radially inward" mean toward that axis, "outward" and "radially outward" mean away from it, and "circumferential" means about that axis. These terms describe relationships within the clamp and do not require the clamp to be used in any particular attitude.
2	
3	Overall arrangement
4	
5	FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 in the closed condition around a pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. Each of the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 is semicircular, and the two frame halves together surround the pipe 90. The first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are joined at one end, referred to as the hinge end, by a hinge 14, and are releasably joined at the other end, referred to as the latch end, by a releasable latch 16. The hinge 14 permits the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 to be swung apart far enough for the clamp 100 to be passed sideways onto a pipe 90 that is already installed, so that the clamp 100 need not be threaded over a free end of the pipe 90. When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame that is annular about the axis of the clamp 100.
6	
7	Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.
8	
9	The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5. The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, or a conduit that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. The mounting boss 70 is connected neither to the segmented cam ring 20 nor to any jaw carriage 30 and does not participate in the synchronization of the jaw carriages 30. Equipment carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.
10	
11	The segmented cam ring
12	
13	FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20 of the clamp 100, drawn removed from the frame with its segments in the coupled condition. The segmented cam ring 20 comprises a first cam ring segment 22 and a second cam ring segment 24. The first cam ring segment 22 is carried by the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 is carried by the second frame half 12, so that each frame half carries one segment of the ring and each segment travels with its own frame half when the clamp 100 is opened.
14	
15	The first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet at two places, one at the hinge end and one at the latch end. At the hinge end the two segments have complementary coupling faces 26, and at the latch end they have complementary coupling faces 28. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are circumferentially facing drive faces, each pair being shaped so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other through the joint. The faces are brought into engagement by the same motion that closes the frame halves: as the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are swung together about the hinge 14 and the latch 16 is engaged, the complementary coupling faces 26 close on one another at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 close on one another at the latch end.
16	
17	Coupling the segments in this way solves a problem created by splitting the clamp. A clamp that must open from the side cannot carry a continuous drive ring across the split, and a divided drive must otherwise be operated separately in each half, with the result that the two halves advance their jaws by amounts that are not fixed relative to one another. Here the division of the ring is undone by the act of closing the clamp. In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring, and a circumferential input applied to either segment is carried around the whole ring. One input, applied at one point on one frame half, therefore reaches every jaw carriage 30 through a single kinematic element, and the relationship between the jaw carriages 30 is set by the geometry of the ring rather than by the way the clamp is operated. When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken by the closing and opening of the frame halves.
18	
19	The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that rotation of the coupled ring produces inward travel of its jaw carriage 30, the three oblique slots 34 being arranged so that the three jaw carriages 30 travel inwardly in synchronism. The inclination of the oblique slots 34 sets the ratio between the circumferential stroke of the coupled ring and the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.
20	
21	The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch acts as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge of the latch can reach, and it lies at an inclination to the direction in which that wedge advances, so that advance of the wedge moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.
22	
23	The jaw carriages
24	
25	FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30. The frame is channeled to form the annular guide 18, which receives the segmented cam ring 20. The annular guide 18 retains the first cam ring segment 22 on the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 on the second frame half 12, and permits the coupled ring to move circumferentially.
26	
27	The frame is further formed with a radial guide 38 at the position of each jaw carriage 30. Each jaw carriage 30 is received in a respective radial guide 38 and is constrained by the radial guide 38 to move radially with respect to the frame. Each jaw carriage 30 carries a follower 32 that projects from the jaw carriage 30 into a respective one of the oblique slots 34 of the segmented cam ring 20. The follower 32 bears against the sides of the oblique slot 34.
28	
29	The follower 32 is constrained in two ways at once. The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 confines the follower 32 to a path that is inclined to the radial direction. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. Because all three followers 32 are engaged in oblique slots 34 of one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism for as long as the ring turns. The jaw pads 40 therefore close on the pipe together.
30	
31	At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.
32	
33	A carriage return spring 44 acts between each jaw carriage 30 and the frame so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward. When the latch 16 is released and the drive from the latch to the ring drive face 36 is removed, the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward and the jaw pads 40 are retracted from the pipe, and the clamp 100 is left with its jaw carriages 30 retracted and ready for the next installation. Retraction of the jaw carriages 30 clears the jaw pads 40 from the pipe before the frame halves are swung apart.
34	
35	The latch and the force-limiting drive train
36	
37	FIG. 4 shows the latch 16 in fragmentary section. The latch 16 includes a latch housing 58 mounted on the frame at the latch end, a latch handle 50 pivotally mounted on the latch housing 58, a wedge 52 movable in the latch housing 58, and a force-limiting spring stack 54 in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52. The wedge 52 is positioned so that its inclined face bears on the ring drive face 36 of the segmented cam ring 20.
38	
39	The latch 16 has two engaged positions. In a first position, the latch 16 holds the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 closed around the pipe 90 but does not clamp it: the frame is captive on the pipe 90 and cannot fall away, while the jaw carriages 30 remain retracted under their carriage return springs 44. In a second, over-center position, the wedge 52 drives the segmented cam ring 20 and the pipe 90 is clamped. Movement of the latch handle 50 from the first position to the second position advances the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36. The inclined face of the wedge 52 converts that advance into circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20, and the coupled ring turns through its limited stroke, the stroke being limited by the travel available to the wedge 52 between the first and second positions of the latch 16.
40	
41	The force-limiting spring stack 54 answers the problem of what becomes of the operator's remaining handle travel. The jaw pads 40 land on the pipe 90 at some point in the stroke that depends on the diameter of the pipe 90, and the latch handle 50 has still to be carried into its over-center position. If the drive train from the latch handle 50 to the wedge 52 were rigid, that remaining travel would be taken up by whatever part of the assembly yielded first, in practice by driving one jaw farther into the pipe 90 than the others and loading it far more heavily. Additional travel of the latch handle 50 after all three jaw pads 40 have contacted the pipe 90 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54 rather than forcing one jaw carriage 30 farther inward than the others.
42	
43	An indicator pin 56 is coupled to the force-limiting spring stack 54 and projects from the latch housing 58. As the force-limiting spring stack 54 compresses, the indicator pin 56 moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing 58, and the position of the indicator pin 56 with respect to that fixed edge shows the operator when the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered a predetermined compression range. The predetermined compression range is the range of stack compression that corresponds to the clamping force for which the clamp 100 is intended. The indicator pin 56 therefore reports clamp loading mechanically, and what it reports is the state of the force-limiting spring stack 54. It is not a measurement of the diameter of the pipe 90.
44	
45	Operation
46	
47	To install the clamp 100 on a pipe 90, the operator opens the latch 16 and swings the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 apart about the hinge 14. The first cam ring segment 22 stays with the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 stays with the second frame half 12, and the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are separated. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 90 from the side and closes them about the hinge 14. Closing the frame halves brings the complementary coupling faces 26 into engagement at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 into engagement at the latch end, coupling the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 into the coupled ring within the annular guide 18.
48	
49	The operator then moves the latch 16 to its first position, in which the frame is held around the pipe 90 without clamping. The operator moves the latch handle 50 to the second, over-center position. The wedge 52 is driven against the ring drive face 36, the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the sides of the three oblique slots 34 drive the three followers 32, and the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism until the pivoting jaw pads 40 seat on the pipe 90. The remaining travel of the latch handle 50 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54, and the operator watches the indicator pin 56 move relative to the fixed edge of the latch housing 58 and so sees that the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered the predetermined compression range. The latch 16 is left in the over-center position and the clamp 100 is loaded on the pipe 90.
50	
51	To remove the clamp 100, the operator releases the latch 16. The latch handle 50 comes back over center, the wedge 52 retreats from the ring drive face 36, and the force-limiting spring stack 54 is unloaded. The carriage return springs 44 then push the jaw carriages 30 radially outward, so that the jaw pads 40 lift from the pipe 90. Only then are the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 swung apart about the hinge 14 and the clamp 100 taken off the pipe 90. The clamp 100 is undamaged by the cycle and may be installed again on the same pipe or on a pipe of a different diameter within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.
52	
53	Features described above in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features described in connection with another, except where the context makes the combination impossible. The embodiments described are illustrative of the disclosed clamp and are not exhaustive of it, and the scope of protection is defined by the claims that follow rather than by any particular embodiment described here.
54

1	Equipment is frequently attached to the outside of a pipe after the pipe has been installed. Sensors, small tools, brackets, and lengths of conduit all have to be carried on a pipe that cannot be taken out of service, cannot be lifted, and has no free end over which a closed ring could be threaded. A clamp intended for that duty therefore has to open from the side, close around the pipe, and grip it firmly enough that the carried equipment keeps its position, while remaining removable so that the same clamp can be taken off and used again elsewhere.
2	
3	A clamp that opens from the side is split into parts, and the split is what makes the gripping problem difficult. Once the clamp body is divided, any drive element that runs around the body is divided with it. Gripping arrangements that answer this by driving the gripping surfaces of each part separately give up the fixed relationship between the two parts of the drive: the two sides of the clamp advance by amounts that depend on how each side is operated, so the clamp tends to settle off center on the pipe, and the load is shared unevenly between the gripping surfaces. Arrangements that instead pull the split body closed on the pipe, in the manner of a band or a two-bolt saddle, transfer the closing force through the joint at the split and rely on the pipe itself to react the closing motion, so the grip depends on how nearly the bore of the clamp matches the outside diameter of the pipe. Such an arrangement is commonly supplied with liners or inserts machined for one nominal pipe size, and a different pipe size calls for a different insert or a different clamp.
4	
5	Reusable clamping also has to deal with the force the operator applies. A hand lever gives the operator no measure of what has been done to the pipe. When the gripping elements have reached the pipe, further travel of the lever has to go somewhere, and in a rigid drive train it goes into whichever gripping element happens to touch first, so that one gripping surface is loaded far more than the others. Thin walled tube, coated pipe, and lined pipe are all damaged by that kind of concentrated loading, and the operator has no indication that it has occurred. Torque tools and gauges can be added to the installation, but they add a separate instrument to the task and, when they respond to the position of the gripping elements, they report the size of the pipe rather than the force in the grip.
6	
7	What has been lacking is a split clamp in which the drive that advances the gripping elements is itself restored to a single, continuous element by the act of closing the clamp, in which every gripping element is advanced from that one drive so that the gripping elements advance together over a range of pipe sizes, and in which the travel remaining in the operator's lever after the gripping elements have landed on the pipe is absorbed within the clamp and reported to the operator as a loading condition rather than as a dimension.
8

1	A split pipe clamp is disclosed in which the element that advances the gripping jaws is divided with the clamp body but is made continuous again by the act of closing the clamp, so that one latch motion advances every jaw together.
2	
3	In one aspect, a split pipe clamp comprises a first frame half and a second frame half joined at a hinge end by a hinge and releasably joined at a latch end by a latch. In a closed condition the two frame halves define a frame having an annular guide and three radial guides. Three jaw carriages are each slidable radially in a respective one of the radial guides, and each jaw carriage carries a jaw pad that is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. A segmented cam ring is received in the annular guide and comprises a first cam ring segment carried by the first frame half and a second cam ring segment carried by the second frame half. The cam ring segments have complementary coupling faces at the hinge end and complementary coupling faces at the latch end, and those faces engage one another as the frame halves are closed, so that in the closed condition the two segments move in the annular guide as a coupled ring. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the segmented cam ring, each oblique slot being inclined to a radial direction of the frame so that rotation of the coupled ring through a stroke advances the three jaw carriages inwardly in synchronism. A wedge movable by the latch bears on a ring drive face of the segmented cam ring, so that movement of the latch rotates the coupled ring through the stroke, and a carriage return spring biases each jaw carriage outwardly so that releasing the latch retracts the jaws.
4	
5	Because the coupled ring is a single kinematic element spanning both frame halves, the three jaw carriages are not driven independently. One latch motion, applied at one point on one frame half, is distributed by the coupled ring to every jaw carriage, and the jaw pads close on the pipe together. The pivoting concave jaw pads seat on the pipe without an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter.
6	
7	In a further aspect, the latch has a first position in which the frame halves are held around the pipe without clamping and a second, over-center position in which the wedge drives the cam ring and the pipe is clamped, and a force-limiting spring stack lies in the drive train between a latch handle and the wedge. Travel of the handle that remains after all three jaw pads have contacted the pipe compresses the force-limiting spring stack instead of advancing one jaw carriage farther than the others. An indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of a latch housing when the force-limiting spring stack enters a predetermined compression range, giving the operator a mechanical report of clamp loading that is produced by the state of the spring stack and not by the diameter of the pipe.
8	
9	In a further aspect, the frame carries a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, a tool, or a conduit, the mounting boss being connected neither to the segmented cam ring nor to any jaw carriage, so that equipment carried on the frame is outside the path by which the jaws are synchronized.
10	
11	In a further aspect, a method of clamping a pipe comprises opening the latch, swinging the frame halves apart about the hinge, placing the frame halves around a pipe, closing the frame halves so that the complementary coupling faces engage and couple the cam ring segments, moving the latch to the first position, and moving the latch to the second, over-center position so that the wedge rotates the coupled ring and the followers advance the three jaw carriages inwardly in synchronism until the jaw pads seat on the pipe. Releasing the latch unloads the force-limiting spring stack and the carriage return springs retract the jaw carriages before the frame halves are opened.

The following description of embodiments refers to the accompanying drawings. The same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout. Terms of direction are used with respect to the frame of the clamp: the axis of the frame is the axis about which the frame is annular in the closed condition and with which the axis of a clamped pipe substantially coincides, "inward" and "radially inward" mean toward that axis, "outward" and "radially outward" mean away from it, and "circumferential" means about that axis. These terms describe relationships within the clamp and do not require the clamp to be used in any particular attitude.

Overall arrangement

FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 in the closed condition around a pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. Each of the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 is semicircular, and the two frame halves together surround the pipe 90. The first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are joined at one end, referred to as the hinge end, by a hinge 14, and are releasably joined at the other end, referred to as the latch end, by a releasable latch 16. The hinge 14 permits the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 to be swung apart far enough for the clamp 100 to be passed sideways onto a pipe 90 that is already installed, so that the clamp 100 need not be threaded over a free end of the pipe 90. When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame that is annular about the axis of the clamp 100.

Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5. The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, or a conduit that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. The mounting boss 70 is connected neither to the segmented cam ring 20 nor to any jaw carriage 30 and does not participate in the synchronization of the jaw carriages 30. Equipment carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.

The segmented cam ring

FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20 of the clamp 100, drawn removed from the frame with its segments in the coupled condition. The segmented cam ring 20 comprises a first cam ring segment 22 and a second cam ring segment 24. The first cam ring segment 22 is carried by the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 is carried by the second frame half 12, so that each frame half carries one segment of the ring and each segment travels with its own frame half when the clamp 100 is opened.

The first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet at two places, one at the hinge end and one at the latch end. At the hinge end the two segments have complementary coupling faces 26, and at the latch end they have complementary coupling faces 28. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are circumferentially facing drive faces, each pair being shaped so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other through the joint. The faces are brought into engagement by the same motion that closes the frame halves: as the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are swung together about the hinge 14 and the latch 16 is engaged, the complementary coupling faces 26 close on one another at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 close on one another at the latch end.

Coupling the segments in this way solves a problem created by splitting the clamp. A clamp that must open from the side cannot carry a continuous drive ring across the split, and a divided drive must otherwise be operated separately in each half, with the result that the two halves advance their jaws by amounts that are not fixed relative to one another. Here the division of the ring is undone by the act of closing the clamp. In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring, and a circumferential input applied to either segment is carried around the whole ring. One input, applied at one point on one frame half, therefore reaches every jaw carriage 30 through a single kinematic element, and the relationship between the jaw carriages 30 is set by the geometry of the ring rather than by the way the clamp is operated. When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken by the closing and opening of the frame halves.

The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that rotation of the coupled ring produces inward travel of its jaw carriage 30, the three oblique slots 34 being arranged so that the three jaw carriages 30 travel inwardly in synchronism. The inclination of the oblique slots 34 sets the ratio between the circumferential stroke of the coupled ring and the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch acts as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge of the latch can reach, and it lies at an inclination to the direction in which that wedge advances, so that advance of the wedge moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.

The jaw carriages

FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30. The frame is channeled to form the annular guide 18, which receives the segmented cam ring 20. The annular guide 18 retains the first cam ring segment 22 on the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 on the second frame half 12, and permits the coupled ring to move circumferentially.

The frame is further formed with a radial guide 38 at the position of each jaw carriage 30. Each jaw carriage 30 is received in a respective radial guide 38 and is constrained by the radial guide 38 to move radially with respect to the frame. Each jaw carriage 30 carries a follower 32 that projects from the jaw carriage 30 into a respective one of the oblique slots 34 of the segmented cam ring 20. The follower 32 bears against the sides of the oblique slot 34.

The follower 32 is constrained in two ways at once. The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 confines the follower 32 to a path that is inclined to the radial direction. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. Because all three followers 32 are engaged in oblique slots 34 of one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism for as long as the ring turns. The jaw pads 40 therefore close on the pipe together.

At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.

A carriage return spring 44 acts between each jaw carriage 30 and the frame so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward. When the latch 16 is released and the drive from the latch to the ring drive face 36 is removed, the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward and the jaw pads 40 are retracted from the pipe, and the clamp 100 is left with its jaw carriages 30 retracted and ready for the next installation. Retraction of the jaw carriages 30 clears the jaw pads 40 from the pipe before the frame halves are swung apart.

The latch and the force-limiting drive train

FIG. 4 shows the latch 16 in fragmentary section. The latch 16 includes a latch housing 58 mounted on the frame at the latch end, a latch handle 50 pivotally mounted on the latch housing 58, a wedge 52 movable in the latch housing 58, and a force-limiting spring stack 54 in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52. The wedge 52 is positioned so that its inclined face bears on the ring drive face 36 of the segmented cam ring 20.

The latch 16 has two engaged positions. In a first position, the latch 16 holds the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 closed around the pipe 90 but does not clamp it: the frame is captive on the pipe 90 and cannot fall away, while the jaw carriages 30 remain retracted under their carriage return springs 44. In a second, over-center position, the wedge 52 drives the segmented cam ring 20 and the pipe 90 is clamped. Movement of the latch handle 50 from the first position to the second position advances the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36. The inclined face of the wedge 52 converts that advance into circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20, and the coupled ring turns through its limited stroke, the stroke being limited by the travel available to the wedge 52 between the first and second positions of the latch 16.

The force-limiting spring stack 54 answers the problem of what becomes of the operator's remaining handle travel. The jaw pads 40 land on the pipe 90 at some point in the stroke that depends on the diameter of the pipe 90, and the latch handle 50 has still to be carried into its over-center position. If the drive train from the latch handle 50 to the wedge 52 were rigid, that remaining travel would be taken up by whatever part of the assembly yielded first, in practice by driving one jaw farther into the pipe 90 than the others and loading it far more heavily. Additional travel of the latch handle 50 after all three jaw pads 40 have contacted the pipe 90 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54 rather than forcing one jaw carriage 30 farther inward than the others.

An indicator pin 56 is coupled to the force-limiting spring stack 54 and projects from the latch housing 58. As the force-limiting spring stack 54 compresses, the indicator pin 56 moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing 58, and the position of the indicator pin 56 with respect to that fixed edge shows the operator when the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered a predetermined compression range. The predetermined compression range is the range of stack compression that corresponds to the clamping force for which the clamp 100 is intended. The indicator pin 56 therefore reports clamp loading mechanically, and what it reports is the state of the force-limiting spring stack 54. It is not a measurement of the diameter of the pipe 90.

Operation

To install the clamp 100 on a pipe 90, the operator opens the latch 16 and swings the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 apart about the hinge 14. The first cam ring segment 22 stays with the first frame half 10 and the second cam ring segment 24 stays with the second frame half 12, and the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are separated. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 90 from the side and closes them about the hinge 14. Closing the frame halves brings the complementary coupling faces 26 into engagement at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 into engagement at the latch end, coupling the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 into the coupled ring within the annular guide 18.

The operator then moves the latch 16 to its first position, in which the frame is held around the pipe 90 without clamping. The operator moves the latch handle 50 to the second, over-center position. The wedge 52 is driven against the ring drive face 36, the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the sides of the three oblique slots 34 drive the three followers 32, and the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism until the pivoting jaw pads 40 seat on the pipe 90. The remaining travel of the latch handle 50 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54, and the operator watches the indicator pin 56 move relative to the fixed edge of the latch housing 58 and so sees that the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered the predetermined compression range. The latch 16 is left in the over-center position and the clamp 100 is loaded on the pipe 90.

To remove the clamp 100, the operator releases the latch 16. The latch handle 50 comes back over center, the wedge 52 retreats from the ring drive face 36, and the force-limiting spring stack 54 is unloaded. The carriage return springs 44 then push the jaw carriages 30 radially outward, so that the jaw pads 40 lift from the pipe 90. Only then are the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 swung apart about the hinge 14 and the clamp 100 taken off the pipe 90. The clamp 100 is undamaged by the cycle and may be installed again on the same pipe or on a pipe of a different diameter within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

Features described above in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features described in connection with another, except where the context makes the combination impossible. The embodiments described are illustrative of the disclosed clamp and are not exhaustive of it, and the scope of protection is defined by the claims that follow rather than by any particular embodiment described here.
